not_established: That any bytes can be put into md1: the bulk-OUT receive path does not exist yet (NAT-076) and the loader's clear plan skipped the reserve; whether the kernel can read a 2.3 GiB ramdisk (NAT-077).
The host-to-phone transfer rate and whether the root fits in the cap; whether anything feeds the 83 s watchdog while the kernel runs free (this run's kernel part lasted about 30 s after the jump).
That the 1.61 GiB left free (105775 x 16 KiB) after the reserve is enough for launchd + dyld + the shared cache (the loader's window ceiling is 4 GiB, Android sees 7.06 GiB).
That Apple's dyld, launchd or any Apple userland runs; the probe is the project's test init.
The exact absolute kernel clock rate (stamps about 2.4 % inflated, not re-measured).
findings: Decision 0029's pass rule is a conjunction of four conditions and all held; the return came 0.2 s above the narrower predicted band (+173.2..+177.7 s) and inside the rule's window (+165..+195 s). The 3.84 s gap between 1209:0001 vanishing and Download Mode reproduces NAT-068's 3.8 s.

The return-class discrimination works as designed: a run that does not pet would have ended as SEC_UPLOAD at about +95 s; this one ended in Download Mode, so the pet is the reason the phone lived about 80 s longer than the unpetted hardware watchdog allows.

Window size, not the reserve, is the memory constraint: after md1 the kernel has 1.61 GiB free; lifting the loader's 4 GiB ceiling (Android sees 7.06 GiB) or shrinking the root becomes a design decision before launchd runs.
